Additionally, five delayed projects from PDP8 are listed, including Nam Dinh I at 1,200 MW and Quang Tri at 1,320 MW with a proposed gas conversion.

Now looking at the operational and near-term plants: Vung Ang II is expected to begin commercial operation in July 2025 with 1,200-1,330 MW capacity under a Mitsubishi/KEPCO partnership. Van Phong I has been operating since 2023-2024 with 1,432 MW but isn't running at full capacity yet, and Aboitiz is acquiring a 25% stake. Na Duong I is a smaller 100 MW facility that's already online.

For plants still in development, Na Duong II is under construction at 110 MW with financing secured as of November 2024. However, Song Hau II has been cancelled according to IEA assessments. The broader picture shows Vietnam had roughly 24.7 GW of coal capacity as of early 2023 with about 6.1 GW under construction, and approximately 30 coal-fired plants are currently operating.

Continuing through the coal plant inventory with Hải Phòng 1 and 2, both 600 MW subcritical units operated by GENCO2 coming online in the late 2000s and early 2010s, followed by Quảng Ninh 1 and 2 under GENCO1 with similar specifications and timing.

Now I'm checking what other plants might be missing from my analysis by reviewing the PDP7A and PDP8 documents.

Now I'm ready to compile everything into a structured working inventory of all the coal plants I've identified, documenting their attributes, operational status, source references, and flagging any remaining uncertainties.

Looking at the coal plants documented in the 2011 EVN annual report, I'm compiling a list of the major units across the system, noting that some plants like Hai Phong I and Quang Ninh I had only one unit commissioned by that point.
